articles.headline: President, PM condole martyrdom of 10 policemen in Kohat, vow to continue fight against terrorism
articles.summary: AI summary: KP Police said 10 personnel, including a DSP, and 18 attackers died when a police team returning from an anti-illegal-mining operation near Kohat was ambushed, which police blamed on TTP militants. President Zardari and PM Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack and pledged to keep fighting terrorism in a province under governor's rule since October 11.

articles.headline: Punjab govt insists smog 'not a political issue' as Lahore, New Delhi gasp for air
articles.summary: AI summary: With Lahore ranked the world's most polluted city (AQI 358) ahead of New Delhi, Punjab minister Marriyum Aurangzeb called smog a scientific and health problem rather than a political one and claimed air quality has improved sharply since 2024. Punjab's EPA said air from India after Diwali affected around half the province, while noting local emissions and weather also contribute.

economic.reason: Smog closed motorway sections and weighs on transport, health costs and outdoor activity.

political.reason: Official messaging and cross-border attribution, with no direct effect on governance stability.

social.reason: Hazardous air quality across Lahore and Punjab poses a serious public health burden.

market.reason: Little direct relevance to investment decisions.

lean.reason: The minister's improvement claims are presented as her statements, alongside EPA data and Indian counterclaims; no Pakistani critics are quoted.

confidence.reason: Full article read; AQI figures are concrete, but the improvement percentages are unverified official claims.

articles.headline: FBR deploys AI to detect discrepancies in tax returns
articles.summary: AI summary: Through SRO 2098 of 2026, the FBR has formalised an automated system that cross-checks individual tax returns against data it already holds and flags mismatches before any penal action. Taxpayers get electronic notices via IRIS with at least seven days to respond, plus a further seven-day reminder if they do not.

economic.reason: Could improve tax compliance and revenue, but also adds scrutiny for filers; net effect unclear.

political.reason: An administrative procedure change with no bearing on institutional stability.

social.reason: Affects individual taxpayers procedurally, with built-in response windows before penalties.

market.reason: Relevant to taxpayers, tax advisers and businesses tracking FBR enforcement.

lean.reason: A straightforward description of a notified rule, without advocacy either way.

confidence.reason: Full article read, describing a published SRO with specific procedural details.

articles.headline: FCC dismisses pleas seeking super tax order review
articles.summary: AI summary: A three-member Federal Constitutional Court bench led by Chief Justice Amin-ud-Din Khan rejected review petitions against its ruling that upheld the super tax under Sections 4B and 4C, saying petitioners were simply re-arguing settled issues. The court also said Supreme Court rulings are only persuasive for it after the 27th Amendment.

economic.reason: Keeps the super tax burden in place on high-income companies and individuals, including retrospective application from Tax Year 2022.

political.reason: A final judicial ruling that settles rather than unsettles the legal position.

social.reason: Little direct effect on daily life for most citizens.

market.reason: Directly affects corporate tax liabilities and earnings expectations for large firms.

lean.reason: Reports the court's reasoning factually without favouring a side.

confidence.reason: Full article read on a clear, reported court decision.

articles.headline: Counsel for Sindh govt tells FCC: SIDC was levied to develop road infrastructure
articles.summary: AI summary: Defending the Sindh Infrastructure Development Cess before the FCC, the Sindh government's counsel Farooq H Naek argued it is a fee funding provincial road infrastructure, not a tax on trade, and asked the court to uphold the 2017 law. Judges asked whether goods arriving by air, sea, pipeline or rail would be covered, and the hearing was adjourned to Thursday.

articles.headline: Fuel prices slashed once again; high-speed diesel cut by Rs7 per litre, petrol by Rs3
articles.summary: AI summary: An Ogra notification cut petrol by Rs3 to Rs335 per litre and high-speed diesel by Rs7 to Rs364, effective November 12, while government levies of Rs114 on petrol and Rs100 on diesel stay in place. Prices are being revised frequently in line with global oil swings tied to US-Iran hostilities, and remain well below April's peak.

economic.reason: Lower diesel and petrol prices ease transport and production costs and may soften inflation.

market.reason: Fuel prices feed directly into inflation, transport and business cost calculations.
